title: When Topology Betrays Privacy: Lattice-Based Reconstruction Attacks on Secure Aggregation in Decentralized Federated Learning
abstract: arXiv:2609.08476v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Secure Aggregation (SA) is widely regarded as a strong defense against model-update leakage in Federated Learning (FL), as it reveals only aggregate results while hiding individual updates. In Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL), SA is commonly instantiated as local neighborhood aggregation, where each node obtains a weighted aggregate over its neighbors. We show that this locality creates a structural leakage surface: sparse decentralized topologies provide colluding semi-honest nodes with asymmetric aggregate views, exposing multiple hidden linear combinations of honest participants' private states. Reconstructing private states from these aggregate views is fundamentally challenging, as both the private states and the aggregation coefficients are hidden. translated_title: 当拓扑背叛隐私：去中心化联邦学习中针对安全聚合的基于格的重构攻击
translated_abstract: 安全聚合（Secure Aggregation, SA）被广泛视为抵御联邦学习（FL）中模型更新泄露的强大防御手段，因为它只揭示聚合结果而隐藏个体更新。在去中心化联邦学习（DFL）中，SA通常被实例化为局部邻域聚合，即每个节点获得其邻居节点上的加权聚合结果。我们证明这种局部性会造成一个结构性的泄露面：稀疏的去中心化拓扑为相互合谋的半诚实节点提供了非对称的聚合视图，从而暴露了诚实参与者隐私状态的多个隐藏线性组合。从这些聚合视图中重构隐私状态在本质上是极具挑战性的，因为隐私状态和聚合系数均处于隐藏状态。为应对这一挑战，我们建立了该问题与隐藏子集和问题（Hidden Subset Sum Problem）这一密码学中长期研究问题之间的形式化联系。基于这一表述，我们设计了一种基于格的…（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 去中心化联邦学习中稀疏拓扑使局部安全聚合成为结构性泄露面，本文通过将重构问题归约为隐藏子集和问题并设计基于格的攻击算法，使合谋的半诚实节点能够重构诚实参与者的私有模型更新。
en_tdlr: Sparse decentralized topologies turn local secure aggregation into a structural leakage surface; this work reduces the reconstruction problem to the Hidden Subset Sum Problem and designs lattice-based attacks that enable colluding semi-honest nodes to recover honest participants' private states.
